inspiration: Doom 3 GUI scripting: menus, the PDA, the HUD and in-world screens are written in a small GUI script language, not in code. A layout can be changed by a designer without a rebuild. Ref: docs/GUIs.md line 3.

Anchor sets per screen shape: custom windows are pinned to top-left, top, centre or a side, with separate variants for 4:3, wide, high and letterboxed screens, so the HUD holds its place on every shape. Ref: docs/img/d3gui-cst-tl-wide.png, d3gui-cst-top-43.png, d3gui-example-16_9-letterbox.png.
Vector source for layouts: the same anchor layouts also come as .svg files (for example d3gui-cst-tl-wide.svg, d3gui-cst-bl-high.svg), so the diagrams can be edited and rescaled. Ref: docs/img/*.svg.
On and off icon pairs in the editor toolbar: a state is shown by a pair of icons that differ in fill or outline, not by text. Ref: neo/sys/win32/rc/res/me_on_icon.ico and me_off_icon.ico.

View-mode toolbar: a row of simple icons switches the viewer between diffuse, specular, normals, skeleton, triangle and overdraw views, the way an artist checks a model. Ref: neo/tools/Help/images/diffuse.png, specular.png, showbones.png, showtris.png.

Depth-fail stencil shadows: the README describes the depth-fail method, restored in dhewm3 1.5.1, as a crisp shadow-volume look. This is an effect technique, not art. Ref: README.md lines 204 to 210 (code, no image).

briefs.label: Anchored HUD layout kit
briefs.why: Windows pinned to fixed anchors keep their place when the screen shape changes, so one layout works at wide, high and letterboxed sizes.
briefs.keep: Anchor set (top-left, top, centre, side); a separate variant per screen shape; a letterbox test case.
briefs.change: Our own grid and anchor points (for example bottom-anchored panels); our own proportions; our own panel corner.

briefs.label: On and off toolbar icon pair
briefs.why: A pair of icons that differ only in fill tells the state at a glance in a dense toolbar.
briefs.keep: Two-state icon pairs; simple shapes; the same size for both states.
briefs.change: Our own icon metaphors; a different state cue (colour or a small badge) instead of fill alone.

briefs.label: Artist view-mode strip
briefs.why: A strip of view-mode icons lets an artist check a model in several passes with one click each.
briefs.keep: Row of view-mode icons; one icon per pass (diffuse, specular, skeleton, triangles).
briefs.change: Our own pass names and icons; add a normals pass with its own glyph.
